opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, admin requires the employee's role to own the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst, so access is capped at write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin for Payroll exceeds max, so cap at read. Recommend granting read.
reason: E002 (Erika Bolton) requested admin access to Payroll. The two team notes conflict on employment type (full-time Analyst vs. contractor with basic security training). Under either profile, admin is not permitted: full-time Analyst does not own Payroll (owned by Payroll Specialist), so the cap is write; a contractor with only basic training is capped at read. Given the conflicting facts, the safe/conservative decision is to grant the lower cap, read, which never exceeds the requested level and stays within policy.
